description: The kit's defaults for your choices (the same on every PC model; hardware lives in profiles/). Don't edit this file: put only the fields you want to change, in the same layout, into config/settings.local.json (git ignores it, so a git pull never touches it). Build-Iso.ps1 lays your file over this one, checks the result and stages it as C:\ProgramData\W11Kit\settings.json, which PostInstall and the validator follow. Keyboard (inputLocale), formats (userLocale), systemLocale, timeZone and homeLocation: where your file doesn't set them, Run-Build.cmd takes them from the PC you build on; the values below are used only when Build-Iso.ps1 is started directly (a CI job), with a note. computerName null: the profile's name, else Windows picks a random one. accounts.builtinAdministratorName / builtinGuestName null: a new pair of names for every build. options.smartAppControl: "leave" (Windows decides) or "off". reminders.expectedApps: apps the validator lists until they are installed, e.g. { "name": "7-Zip", "wingetId": "7zip.7zip" }. docs/reference/CONFIGURATION.md explains every field. options.windowsUpdateDrivers: true lets Windows Update deliver driver and firmware updates for existing devices (new devices still search no online source). options.optionalUpdates: "off", "auto" or "userChoice". options.controlledFolderAccess and options.asrPrevalenceRule ("block", "audit", "off"): Defender's ransomware protection on the installed PC; Run-Build.cmd asks before pausing them for a build. options.asrExclusions: full paths of folders or programs ("C:\Tools\runner") that Defender's two reputation rules (the prevalence rule and the ransomware rule) let run; every other ASR rule still covers them. options.scheduledValidation: true runs the validator by itself, weekly and after a Windows Update restart, and shows a row that has newly turned FAIL. options.netbios: "off" or "leave". options.firstNetworkCategory: "public" (Windows' default) or "private" for the network Setup used (on Public, firewall rules that apps add themselves have no effect). options.idleHibernate: false = the PC never hibernates or sleeps by itself (a desktop that also serves). options.dns.overHttps: "leave" or "require" (then servers = [{ "address", "template" }], each DNS over HTTPS only, and localZones = [{ "namespace": ".lan", "servers": ["192.168.1.1"] }] for names only your own network knows). accounts.expectedExtra: local accounts you add on purpose (the validator then accepts them).
